title: Leray spectral sequence
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes and $\mathcal F$ a
quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module. There is a spectral sequence

$$
E_2^{p,q}=\mathrm H^p\bigl(Y,R^qf_*\mathcal F\bigr)
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \mathrm H^{p+q}(X,\mathcal F).
$$

(*Stacks Project, Cohomology of Sheaves, Lemma 20.13.4, Tag
[01F2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01F2).*)

proof.text: Put $F=f_*:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)\to\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_Y)$ and $G=\Gamma(Y,-):\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_Y)\to\mathbf{Ab}$. The module categories are Grothendieck abelian, hence have enough injectives, by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], and $\mathbf{Ab}=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathbb Z)$ is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-grothendieck-abelian] with $R=\mathbb Z$. The pushforward $F$ is the additive functor of [def-pc-module-pullback]; for a kernel or finite product, its sections on an open $V\subseteq Y$ are the corresponding kernel or product of sections on $f^{-1}(V)$, so $F$ preserves kernels and finite products and is left exact. The global-sections functor $G$ is additive and left exact by [lem-sc-global-sections-left-exact]. For every injective $\mathcal I$ on $X$, [lem-weil-pbc-module-pushforward-injective-acyclic] says that $f_*\mathcal I$ is $G$-acyclic. Thus $(F,G)$ satisfies [def-sp-composite-acyclicity].

source.place: ## Proof, application of the Grothendieck spectral sequence

proof.text: Apply [thm-sp-grothendieck] to this composable pair and the object $\mathcal F$. It gives a functorial first-quadrant spectral sequence with $E_2^{p,q}=R^pG(R^qF(\mathcal F))$ converging to $R^{p+q}(G\circ F)(\mathcal F)$.

source.place: ## Proof, application of the Grothendieck spectral sequence

proof.text: By [pqf-def-cohomology], $R^qF(\mathcal F)=R^qf_*\mathcal F$ and $R^pG(-)=\mathrm H^p(Y,-)$. Termwise $\Gamma(Y,f_*\mathcal G)=\Gamma(X,\mathcal G)$, so the composite is global sections on $X$ and its right derived functors are $\mathrm H^{p+q}(X,\mathcal F)$; resolution-independent identification is supplied by [lem-sp-derived-well-defined]. Substitution gives the displayed Leray spectral sequence.
